issues.issue: The report's own schedules say what this 22,548 is: the Statement of Activities (p2) prints it as 'Electric, gas, and cable lease' under general revenues, and the budget schedule (p11) prints it as 'Franchise Fees 22,548'. So occupation/franchise tax fits better than charges for services. Same for detail[6].

A '5% gross' receipt is usually the public power district payment of 5% of gross revenue (the rules list 'NPPD 5%' under Public Power District Sales Tax). The Statement of Activities groups it with program charges (8,614 = 3,540 + 1,074 + 4,000). The category is a guess either way. Same for detail[4].

The whole amount is in the Street Fund column, and the 'listed by object' rule (use the fund's function) would make it streets/highways, as was done for Supplies and materials 15,347. The Operating category is meant only for lines that would otherwise be other.
This object line mixes two funds. general government is the larger share but isn't the function of 41% of the line.
The label names one function, but 27,377 of it is Street Fund (streets/highways) capital outlay.
The grantor isn't stated. The budget schedule groups it as 'Grants, donations and misc.', so it could be a donation or a federal grant. Same for detail[44].

issues.issue: Under the 2026-10-27 balance-sheet rule, governmental lines come from the governmental funds statement (fund balance by classification: Restricted (69,843), Unassigned 107,601) when its totals equal the government-wide figures, as they do here. The extraction instead uses the government-wide Total column with Restricted/Unrestricted net position.
